transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um, well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but... I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that my eating has been a little all over the place lately. I mean, I'm sure it's not the worst thing in the world, but some weeks I just barely touch my dinner. And then other nights... well, it's a little embarrassing, but I end up just standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone’s gone to bed. 

I feel a bit silly even mentioning it, to be honest. Is that... is that the kind of thing I should be telling you?
When you find yourself eating those crackers and sweets late at night, do you feel like you can control how much you eat, or does it feel like you can't stop once you've started?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I can't stop. It's not like that, I promise. Um, like I was saying before, it's really just that my appetite has been so up and down lately. So when I'm having those crackers and sweets, it's more like... I'm just finally hungry because I barely touched my dinner on those other nights. 

I definitely have control, it's just... maybe a little bit of a bad habit I've let myself fall into? I just kind of lose track of how many I've had because it's quiet and I'm finally relaxing. I really hope that doesn't make me sound awful. Does that make sense, or am I explaining it poorly?
When you're eating those crackers and sweets late at night, would you say you're eating a noticeably larger amount of food than most people would eat in that same time period?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say it's a huge amount. Really, I'm sure it's not more than anyone else might have for a little late-night snack. It's just a handful of crackers, maybe a few cookies. I mean, it's not like I'm clearing out the pantry or anything like that. 

I just... I worry I'm making a bigger deal out of it than it is. It's just a few extra bites because I didn't eat much earlier in the day. That's pretty normal, right? I'm trying to be good about it, I really am. I hope it doesn't seem like I'm just stuffing my face.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling sad, down, or depressed most of the time? Or have you noticed that things you normally enjoy don't seem as fun or interesting anymore?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I'm depressed. That sounds so serious, doesn't it? But, um, I guess I do go through these stretches sometimes where... I don't know, the house just feels kind of gray and heavy? 

Like, I'll just sit at the kitchen table and feel a bit empty inside, even though nothing terrible has happened that day. It's probably just normal mood swings, right? Everyone gets a little down sometimes. I try really hard to shake it off so I'm not a bother to anyone. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I'm not trying to make it sound worse than it is, I promise.

Over these past few weeks when you've been feeling that heaviness and emptiness, have you also been experiencing worry or anxiety about things—maybe things that feel hard to control or that keep coming back to your mind?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, I worry a little bit, but just normal things, you know? Like making sure the bills are paid or if I remembered to lock the door. Nothing that keeps me up at night or feels out of control. 

I really try not to be an anxious person. I think I handle stress pretty well, actually. I just try to take a deep breath and move on. It's not like I'm sitting around panicking all day. That's a good thing, right? I'm doing okay with that part, at least?
Have you noticed any changes in your weight over these past few weeks—either gaining or losing weight? And if so, has that been something that's been concerning to you?

Um, well... I haven't really been weighing myself, so I'm not exactly sure about the numbers. But I guess my clothes might be fitting a tiny bit differently? 

It's just that my eating has been a little... unpredictable lately. Some weeks I just don't have much of an appetite, so I might barely touch dinner. And then, like we were talking about earlier, other nights I'll be up late having some crackers and sweets in the kitchen after everyone is asleep. 

That's actually kind of what finally pushed me to come in and talk to someone. I just want to make sure I'm taking care of myself properly. It's not a huge, dramatic weight change, though. I'm trying to keep a good balance. That's the right thing to do, isn't it? Just keeping an eye on it so it doesn't get out of hand?
When you're not eating, do you find yourself thinking a lot about food, your weight, or how your body looks? Does that occupy much of your thinking throughout the day?

Oh, no, no, definitely not. I don't obsess over my weight or anything like that. I mean, I know some women my age really struggle with that sort of thing, but I've always tried to just be grateful for the body I have, you know? 

I don't spend my day staring in the mirror or counting calories or worrying about how I look. It's really just that my appetite is a bit... inconsistent right now. I'm not trying to diet or anything on purpose. I'd never want to do anything unhealthy like that. I just want to feel well and be healthy. That's the most important thing, right? Being healthy on the inside?

When you're having those stretches where the house feels gray and heavy, and your eating changes—how long do those periods typically last? Are we talking about a few days, a couple of weeks, or longer?

Um, well... I guess if I really sit down and add it all up, those... those gray periods, where everything just feels so heavy and I feel so guilty for not wanting to do anything... it's probably been about seven months total. 

I know that sounds like a long time, but it's not all at once! It comes and goes. I really do try to push through it and keep things normal for everyone else. I don't just lay in bed the whole time, I promise. I try to keep up with things as best I can. Seven months isn't too terrible, is it? I mean, I'm here now, trying to get it sorted out, so that's a good step, right?

During these seven months, have there been any stretches where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep than normal, or felt especially upbeat or optimistic—almost the opposite of those gray, heavy periods?

Um, well... yes, actually. I do have times where I feel the exact opposite of the gray. Sometimes I have these wonderful stretches where I feel just... bright, you know? Like I'm completely unstoppable and I can get so much done around the house. It's actually such a relief to feel that way. 

But... um... I guess I should mention—and I feel a little terrible admitting this, because I really try to be a good wife—sometimes during those really energetic stretches, I can get suddenly furious over just... really small things. Like, if my husband moves my paints while he's tidying up, or if he just innocently questions a receipt from the store... I might just snap at him out of nowhere. 

I always apologize right away, of course! I don't like being that way at all, and I'd never want you to think I'm an angry person. I think it's just that I have all this energy and I get a little too focused on what I'm doing. It's just a little bit of stress coming out, right? Everyone gets a little snappy sometimes when they have a lot going on... don't they?

During those bright, energetic stretches when you feel unstoppable and can get so much done, do you find that you need less sleep than usual? Like, are you sleeping maybe 4-5 hours instead of your normal 7-8 hours, but still feeling rested and energized?

Well... yes, I suppose I do sleep a bit less during those times. But it's not like I'm tossing and turning or suffering from insomnia! It's actually quite nice. I can sleep maybe three or four hours and wake up feeling completely charged and ready to go. 

I'll be up before the sun, writing blog posts or planning out all these new projects for the house. It just feels like I have so much extra time to be productive, you know? I'm not tired at all during the day when that happens. It just means I'm making the most of my time, right? There's nothing wrong with being a morning person, is there?
